nanotyrannus:eswiki:7.title: Nanotyrannus (Controversia: T. rex inmaduro o género separado)

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus fossils date to the Late Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Maastrichtian

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lived in western North America 67 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus (/ˈnænoʊˌtaɪˌrænəs, -tɪ- /, ) is a genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaur that lived in what is now western North America during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, 67 million years ago.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus fossils are primarily found in the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: Its fossils are mainly known from the Hell Creek Formation.

facts.statement: The species N. lancensis was first described in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore as a new species of Gorgosaurus.
facts.quote: The first named species, N. lancensis, was described as a new species of Gorgosaurus in 1946 by Charles W. Gilmore based on a single skull.

facts.statement: In 1988, Robert T. Bakker, Michael Williams, and Philip J. Currie reclassified the species into the new genus Nanotyrannus due to its small size.
facts.quote: Re-examination of the specimen in 1988 by Robert T. Bakker, Michael Williams and Philip J. Currie moved the species to a new genus of tyrannosaurid, named Nanotyrannus in reference to its small body size compared to other tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: Many researchers believe the original Nanotyrannus skull belongs to an immature Tyrannosaurus rex rather than a distinct species.
facts.quote: Subsequent research indicated that the skull belonged to an immature animal, leading many researchers to favor its identification as a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: In 2025, Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli argued that the "Bloody Mary" specimen is a mature individual of N. lancensis, supporting the validity of the genus.
facts.quote: In 2025, Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli published an exhaustive revision of Nanotyrannus. Therein, they described a complete tyrannosauroid skeleton from the Hell Creek Formation, also known by its nicknames "Bloody Mary" and "Manteo" (part of the Dueling Dinosaurs specimen), which they demonstrated to be a mature N. lancensis individual.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid measuring approximately 17 feet in length.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid, measuring around 17 ft in length.

facts.statement: Unlike Tyrannosaurus, Nanotyrannus possessed a slender, low skull with small crests or horns in front of its eyes.
facts.quote: Unlike Tyrannosaurus, Nanotyrannus had a slender, low skull, and small crests or horns immediately in front of its eyes.

facts.statement: The rear teeth were serrated and laterally compressed in a condition called ziphodonty, which is not seen in tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The rest of the teeth were serrated and compressed from side to side, a condition known as ziphodonty, which is not seen in tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had longer legs than contemporaries, suggesting it was a pursuit predator, and possessed forelimbs that were larger both absolutely and proportionally than its relatives.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus was longer-legged than contemporary taxa, suggesting that it was a pursuit predator, and had forelimbs which were both absolutely and proportionally larger than its relatives.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Nanotyrannus is skull CMNH 7541, collected in 1942 by David Hosbrook Dunkle.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus is based on CMNH 7541, a skull collected in 1942 by David Hosbrook Dunkle.

facts.statement: The name Nanotyrannus was derived from Latin words meaning "small tyrant".
facts.quote: They named the new genus Nanotyrannus for the specimen, stating that the name derives from the Latin words nano, meaning small, and tyrannus, meaning tyrant.

facts.statement: The etymology of Nanotyrannus has been clarified to derive from Greek words meaning "dwarf king".
facts.quote: The etymology has subsequently been clarified to be derived from the Greek words νάνος (nanos), meaning dwarf or pygmy, and τύραννος (tyrannos), meaning king.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that the holotype was a juvenile T. rex was first suggested in 1965 by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky.
facts.quote: The possibility that the holotype represents a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex was first suggested by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky in 1965.

facts.statement: In 1999, Thomas Carr analyzed the specimen and concluded it was immature, supporting the view that it is a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Subsequent analysis of the specimen by Thomas Carr in 1999 indicated that it was immature, leading Carr and many other paleontologists to consider it a juvenile specimen of T. rex.

facts.statement: News reports in late 2011 covered a 2006 discovery of a nearly complete tyrannosaur specimen found with a ceratopsid.
facts.quote: In late 2011, news reports about a 2006 discovery of a new, virtually complete tyrannosaur specimen found alongside a ceratopsid were made.

facts.statement: The "Bloody Mary" fossil was acquired by the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences in 2020.
facts.quote: The fossil was acquired by the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences in 2020, after which the museum built an additional research lab space in which to prepare, study, and display the specimens.

facts.statement: Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli published an initial description of the "Bloody Mary" specimen in 2025.
facts.quote: In 2025, paleontologists Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli published an initial description of the "Bloody Mary" specimen as part of an extensive revision of the genus Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: Roberts et al. (2026) dated the origin of the Hell Creek Formation locality to approximately 66.897 million years ago.
facts.quote: Roberts et al. (2026) identified their locality of origin as the lower portion of the Hell Creek Formation, dated to approximately 66.897 million years ago.

facts.statement: Large muscle attachment sites at the back of the skull suggest Nanotyrannus could strongly flex its head side to side.
facts.quote: The muscle attachment sites at the back of its skull were large, suggesting that it could strongly flex its head from side to side.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus morphology combines traits from basal tyrannosauroids like Moros and Xiongguanlong with those of derived tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The morphology of Nanotyrannus combines characteristics from more basal tyrannosauroids, such as Moros and Xiongguanlong, with more derived tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: N. lethaeus was larger than N. lancensis, with mature individuals potentially reaching 1200 kg.
facts.quote: N. lethaeus was larger, and mature individuals may have reached a body mass of about 1200 kg.

facts.statement: The specific name lethaeus references the river Lethe from mythology and the Hell Creek Formation where the specimen was found.
facts.quote: The specific name for the second species, lethaeus, comes from the Latin, and is the adjective of Lethe, referring to the river Lethe from Greco-Roman mythology, which flows through the underworld (often equated to hell). The name references both the Hell Creek Formation, where the specimen was found, and the mythological function of drinking from the Lethe: to forget a prior life and be reincarnated.

facts.statement: Some scientists argue that Nanotyrannus is distinct from Tyrannosaurus because it has 15-16 teeth on each side of the upper jaw and 16-18 on each side of the lower jaw, while adult T. rex has 11-12 upper and 12-14 lower teeth.
facts.quote: Specimens referred to N. lancensis have 15-16 teeth on each side of the maxilla (upper jaw) and 16-18 teeth on each side of the dentary (lower jaw), whereas adult T. rex specimens had 11–12 tooth positions in the upper jaw and 12–14 in the lower.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Carr used data from Gorgosaurus showing that tooth count decreases as the animal grows to support the hypothesis that Nanotyrannus is simply a juvenile Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Carr showed that, in Gorgosaurus libratus, the number of teeth decreased as the animal grew, and he used this data to support the hypothesis that N. lancensis is simply a juvenile T. rex.

facts.statement: Yun (2015) claimed that all differences used to distinguish Nanotyrannus were due to individual variation, ontogeny, or taphonomic distortion.
facts.quote: Yun (2015) claimed that all of the differences used to distinguish Nanotyrannus were individually or ontogenetically variable features, or the products of taphonomic distortion of the bones.

facts.statement: Voris et al. (June 2025) suggested that Longrich and Saitta's placement of Nanotyrannus outside Tyrannosauridae was caused by characteristics related to immaturity and problematic data, supporting the view that it is a juvenile T. rex.
facts.quote: Voris et al. (June 2025) suggested that the scoring of Nanotyrannus in a more basal position by Longrich & Saitta (2024) may have been caused by "scoring characteristics related to immaturity" and problematic data sets, supporting the previous interpretation that Nanotyrannus represents a juvenile T. rex.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul (June 2025) supported a basal eutyrannosaurian position for Nanotyrannus as part of his "multiple small taxa hypothesis" for theropod diversity in the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: Later in June 2025, Gregory S. Paul also supported a basal eutyrannosaurian (non-tyrannosaurid) position for Nanotyrannus, emphasizing the validity and distinction of this genus as part of his preferred "multiple small taxa hypothesis" (MSTH) for theropod diversity in the Hell Creek Formation.

facts.statement: In October 2025, Zanno and Napoli affirmed the validity of Nanotyrannus after re-examining the "Bloody Mary" specimen (NCSM 40000).
facts.quote: In October 2025, the validity of Nanotyrannus was affirmed in an extensive paper by Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli, in which the "Bloody Mary" specimen (NCSM 40000) was re-examined.

facts.statement: No known amniotes undergo absolute limb shrinkage; limbs only become proportionally smaller if they grow slower than the rest of the body.
facts.quote: There are no amniotes known to the authors that undergo any degree of absolute limb shrinkage, merely instances where limbs grew slower than the rest of the body and became proportionally smaller.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists who previously doubted Nanotyrannus accepted it as a valid taxon after Zanno and Napoli's paper, specifically agreeing the "Bloody Mary" specimen is distinct from Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Authors who have authored papers questioning Nanotyrannus validity, such as Thomas Carr, Steve Brusatte and David Hone, accepted that the "Bloody Mary" specimen was a distinct species from Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: Thomas Carr and Steve Brusatte objected to classifying the juvenile tyrannosaurid BMRP 2002.4.1 "Jane" as Nanotyrannus lethaeus.
facts.quote: Carr and Brusatte objected to the classification of the juvenile tyrannosaurid BMRP 2002.4.1 "Jane" as Nanotyrannus lethaeus

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that the N. lancensis holotype belongs to a mature individual and is therefore a species distinct from Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: After sampling the hyoids of the N. lancensis holotype, the researchers concluded that it belongs to a mature individual, and thus a species distinct from Tyrannosaurus rex

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus was a mid-sized tyrannosauroid

facts.statement: The holotype skull (CMNH 7541) of Nanotyrannus measures 57.2 cm from the anterior tip of the premaxilla to the posterior tip of the quadrate.
facts.quote: The holotype skull (CMNH 7541) of Nanotyrannus measures 57.2 cm when measured from the anterior (front) tip of the premaxilla to the posterior (rear) tip of the quadrate

facts.statement: The prominent subnarial foramen found in many tyrannosauroids is absent in every specimen of Nanotyrannus.
facts.quote: this is absent in every specimen of Nanotyrannus

facts.statement: The basitubera of Nanotyrannus were strongly laterally expanded, suggesting the head could be strongly flexed sideways.
facts.quote: The basitubera (muscle attachment sites at the back of the head) of Nanotyrannus were strongly laterally expanded, suggesting that the head could be strongly flexed sideways

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus possessed premaxillary teeth that were completely smooth and lacked serrations, a trait shared with other tyrannosauroids like Moros and Timurlengia.
facts.quote: The premaxillary teeth of Nanotyrannus are distinct from those of other tyrannosauroids in that they were completely devoid of serrations, like Moros, Timurlengia, and Xiongguanlong

facts.statement: Each premaxilla bone in Nanotyrannus held exactly four chisel-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: Each premaxilla bore four chisel-shaped teeth.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had between sixteen and eighteen teeth in its lower jaw, a count higher than any tyrannosaurid except Alioramus and Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus has between sixteen and eighteen teeth per dentary, a higher count than in any tyrannosaurid except for Alioramus and Daspletosaurus.

facts.statement: The frontmost tooth in each upper jaw of Nanotyrannus was small and resembled the premaxillary teeth, unlike the large front teeth seen in Daspletosaurus and Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Unlike Daspletosaurus, Tarbosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus, but like many other tyrannosauroids, the most anterior tooth of each maxilla was small and resembled those of the premaxillae.

facts.statement: Unlike most tyrannosaurids, the upper jaw teeth of Nanotyrannus were ziphodont, meaning they had serrations on only one edge.
facts.quote: Unlike most tyrannosaurids, the maxillary teeth were ziphodont.

facts.statement: The skeleton of Nanotyrannus is estimated to have twenty vertebrae before the sacrum and thirty-five vertebrae in the tail.
facts.quote: The vertebral column of Nanotyrannus appears to consist of twenty presacral vertebrae (those before the sacrum), and thirty-five caudal (tail) vertebrae.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus had proportionally very large arms that were more similar to early tyrannosauroids than to later tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The arms of Nanotyrannus are proportionally very large, proportionally more similar to basal tyrannosauroids than to those of tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: The lower end of the upper arm bone in Nanotyrannus featured five tubercles, a feature not found in other eutyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The distal (further from the body) end of the humerus (upper arm bone) of Nanotyrannus bears five tubercles, unlike other eutyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: The hand of Nanotyrannus was functionally two-fingered but retained a vestigial third finger bone, similar to Gorgosaurus.
facts.quote: The manus was functionally didactyl (two-fingered), though it does retain the first phalanx (finger bone) of a vestigial third digit, as in Gorgosaurus

facts.statement: The first finger bone of the second metacarpal in Nanotyrannus possessed a deep extensor pit and a prominent proximal tubercle.
facts.quote: The first phalanx of the second metacarpal of Nanotyrannus bears a deep extensor pit with a prominent proximal tubercle.

facts.statement: The first finger bone of the thumb in Nanotyrannus was nearly twice the size of the equivalent bone in Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The first phalanx of the first manual digit is nearly twice the size of that of the equivalent bone in Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The claw-supporting bones in Nanotyrannus were large, with the second one being laterally compressed.
facts.quote: The ungual phalanges of Nanotyrannus, the bones which would have supported claws in life, were large, and the second was laterally compressed.

facts.statement: Despite its smaller body size, the foot bones of the NCSM 40000 specimen of Nanotyrannus were almost as long as those of the largest Tyrannosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: Despite its body size being far smaller, the metatarsals of NCSM 40000 are almost as long as those of the very largest Tyrannosaurus specimens.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the extremely long hind limbs of Nanotyrannus indicate a lifestyle adapted for pursuit predation, differing from the ambush style of tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: The extreme proportions of their "hypercursorial" hind limbs may correlate to a different lifestyle from tyrannosaurids, one adapted more toward pursuit predation.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the lack of serrations on Nanotyrannus teeth is a sign of juvenile development or a unique diagnostic trait of the species.
facts.quote: whilst the presence or absence of serrations has been suggested to vary with ontogeny, they are likely a diagnostic trait in the case of Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: Recent studies classify Nanotyrannus as a member of the clade Nanotyrannidae, which is the sister taxon to Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Both recovered Nanotyrannus as a member of the Eutyrannosauria in a new clade deemed the Nanotyrannidae, which is the sister taxon to the Tyrannosauridae.

facts.statement: The genus Nanotyrannus was originally described by Bakker, Currie, and Williams in 1988.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Bakker, Currie & Williams, 1988

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Nanotyrannus is Nanotyrannus lancensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Nanotyrannus lancencis

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lancensis has been synonymized with Gorgosaurus lancensis, Deinodon lancensis, Aublysodon lancensis, Albertosaurus lancensis, and Tyrannosaurus lancensis.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Gorgosaurus lancensis Gilmore, 1946 Deinodon lancensis Gilmore, 1946 Aublysodon lancensis Gilmore, 1946 Albertosaurus lancensis Gilmore, 1946 Tyrannosaurus lancensis Gilmore, 1946

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 68 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage of North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente de 68 a 66 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lived in a warm, humid, and swampy environment with maritime to subtropical conditions.
facts.quote: The depositional environment of this region was warm, humid, and swampy environment, reflecting maritime to subtropical conditions.

facts.statement: A 2021 study estimated the bite force of juvenile Tyrannosaurus, including Nanotyrannus 'Jane', to be between 5,269 and 5,641 Newtons, which is higher than previous estimates.
facts.quote: In 2021, Peterson and colleagues also used Jane's maxillary tooth to estimate the bite force of a tyrannosaur that produced the puncture marks on Jane, and concluded that Jane and similarly sized juvenile Tyrannosaurus had a bite force of 5,269-5,641 N, higher than the previously estimated maximum bite force of Jane (2,400-3,850 N) by Bates and Falkingham in 2012.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus specimens have cursorial limb proportion scores significantly higher than adult T. rex, indicating they were more adapted for running.
facts.quote: The CLP scores of Jane and the "Bloody Mary" specimen were 35.8 and 32.7 respectively, which were well above the CLP score of 11.5 for adult T. rex specimens, indicating that Nanotyrannus was more cursorily adapted than T. rex.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus fossils were first discovered in the Hell Creek Formation, which spans Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus was first discovered in the Hell Creek Formation, which spans parts of modern-day Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.

facts.statement: Fossils of Nanotyrannid teeth, potentially belonging to Nanotyrannus, have been found in the Lance Formation.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannid teeth fossils, potentially belonging to Nanotyrannus itself, are known from the Lance Formation.

facts.statement: Researchers note that further testing and more data are required to determine which phylogenetic analysis of Nanotyrannus relationships is correct.
facts.quote: The authors noted that further testing and more data would be required to support the results of one analysis over the other.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus is a medium-sized tyrannosaurid.
facts.quote: Nanotyrannus es un tiranosauroide de tamaño mediano.

facts.statement: The adult N. lancensis specimen known as Bloody Mary may have weighed around 704 kg.
facts.quote: El N. lancensis adulto pudo haber pesado alrededor de 704 kg, según el espécimen de Bloody Mary.

facts.statement: The species N. lethaeus was larger, with mature individuals potentially reaching a body mass of approximately 1200 kg.
facts.quote: N. lethaeus, por su parte, era más grande; los individuos maduros pudieron haber alcanzado una masa corporal de aproximadamente 1200 kg.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus measured around 5.5 meters in length and 2 meters in height, about one-third the size of Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Solo medía alrededor de 5,5 metros de longitud y 2 de altura, un tercio del tamaño de Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus generally had Cretaceous tyrannosaurid characteristics, including a flat, square head about 60 cm long, sharp claws and teeth, and a heavy body.
facts.quote: En general tenía las características de cualquier tiranosáurido del Cretácico, una cabeza chata y cuadrada con un tamaño cercano a los 60 centímetros de largo, contaba con garras y dientes afilados, así como un cuerpo no liviano.

facts.statement: Bakker suggests that due to its weight and build, Nanotyrannus hunted in packs.
facts.quote: Bakker sostiene que, debido a su peso y complexion, Nanotyrannus cazaba en manadas.

facts.statement: Teeth from multiple Nanotyrannus individuals have been found in herbivore bones.
facts.quote: Dientes de múltiples Nanotyrannus han sido encontrados en huesos de herbívoros.

facts.statement: Unlike Tyrannosaurus, Nanotyrannus had a thin, low skull and small crests or horns just in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: A diferencia de Tyrannosaurus, Nanotyrannus tenía un cráneo delgado y bajo, y pequeñas crestas o cuernos justo delante de los ojos.

facts.statement: The front upper jaw teeth were not serrated, while the rest were laterally compressed; this condition known as ziphodonty is not observed in tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Los dientes de la parte frontal de la mandíbula superior no eran serrados, a diferencia del resto, que a su vez se encontraban comprimidos lateralmente; condición conocida como zifodoncia que no se observa en los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: It is represented by a small skull, catalog number CMNH 7541, discovered by Charles W. Gilmore in 1942 and described in 1946 as Gorgosaurus lancensis, also known as Albertosaurus lancensis, and published posthumously.
facts.quote: Representado por un pequeño cráneo, número de catálogo CMNH 7541, descubierto por Charles W. Gilmore en 1942 y descrito en 1946 como un espécimen de Gorgosaurus lancensis, también conocido como Albertosaurus lancensis y publicado póstumamente.

facts.statement: In 1988, the specimen was redescribed by Robert T. Bakker, Phil Currie, and Michael Williams, the curator of the Cleveland Museum of Natural History, where the original specimen is deposited and exhibited.
facts.quote: En 1988, el espécimen fue redescrito por Robert T. Bakker, Phil Currie, y Michael Williams, el curador principal del Museo de Historia Natural de Cleveland, donde el espécimen original está depositado y exhibido.

facts.statement: It was named Nanotyrannus, a new genus derived from the Latin words nano, meaning 'small', and tyrannus, meaning 'tyrant'.
facts.quote: Le dieron el nombre de Nanotyrannus, un nuevo género, derivado de las palabras latinas nano, que significa «pequeño», y tyrannus, que significa «tirano».

facts.statement: It was later clarified that the etymology comes from the Greek words nanos, meaning 'dwarf' or 'pygmy', and tyrannos, meaning 'king'.
facts.quote: Posteriormente se aclaró que la etimología proviene de las palabras griegas νάνος (nanos), que significa «enano» o «pigmeo», y τύραννος (tyrannos), que significa «rey».

facts.statement: The possibility that the holotype represented a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex was first suggested by Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky in 1965.
facts.quote: La posibilidad de que el holotipo representara un Tyrannosaurus rex juvenil fue sugerida por primera vez por Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky en 1965.

facts.statement: The exact implications of this difference in tooth number have been controversial.
facts.quote: Las implicaciones exactas de esta diferencia en el número de dientes ha sido controvertida.

facts.statement: In his 1999 study on tyrannosaurid growth patterns, Carr showed that in Gorgosaurus libratus, the number of teeth decreased as the animal developed, and he used these data to support the hypothesis that N. lancensis is simply a young T. rex.
facts.quote: En su estudio de 1999 sobre los patrones de crecimiento de los tiranosáuridos, Carr mostró que en Gorgosaurus libratus, el número de dientes decrecía conforme el animal se desarrollaba, y él usó estos datos para apoyar la hipótesis de que N. lancensis es simplemente un T. rex joven.

facts.statement: These researchers also noted that there were significant differences in tooth number between individuals of the same age in both Tyrannosaurus and Gorgosaurus, and that tooth number can therefore vary due to individual factors unrelated to growth.
facts.quote: Estos investigadores también notaron que tanto en Tyrannosaurus como en Gorgosaurus había significativas diferencias en el número de dientes entre individuos de las mismas edades, y que el número de dientes por lo tanto puede variar por factores individuales no relacionados con el crecimiento.

facts.statement: A juvenile Tarbosaurus skull discovered in 2006 exhibits the same number of teeth as adult Tarbosaurus skulls, supporting the idea that Nanotyrannus is a different genus.
facts.quote: Un cráneo de un Tarbosaurus juvenil descubierto en 2006 exhibe el mismo número de dientes que los cráneos adultos de Tarbosaurus, apoyando la idea de que Nanotyrannus es un género diferente.

facts.statement: However, many of the differences cited to support the validity of Nanotyrannus are ontogenetic or individually variable traits.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, muchas de las diferencias que se citan para apoyar la validez de Nanotyrannus son rasgos ontogénica o individualmente variables.

facts.statement: In 2013, Carr declared that all differences claimed to support Nanotyrannus turned out to be individual or ontogenetically variable characteristics or products of bone distortion.
facts.quote: En 2013, Carr declaró que todas las diferencias que afirmaban apoyar a Nanotyrannus resultaron ser características individuales u ontogenéticamente variables o productos de distorsión de los huesos.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Manabu Sakomoto has commented that this conclusion is likely affected by the small sample size, and the discrepancy does not necessarily reflect taxonomic distinction.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo Manabu Sakomoto ha comentado que esta conclusión probablemente se ve afectada por el bajo tamaño de la muestra, y la discrepancia no necesariamente refleja la distinción taxonómica.

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lived during the Cretaceous period, sharing the general characteristics of tyrannosaurids of that time.
facts.quote: A diferencia de Tyrannosaurus, Nanotyrannus tenía un cráneo delgado y bajo, y pequeñas crestas o cuernos justo delante de los ojos.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the holotype of Nanotyrannus lancensis might be an immature individual of Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Carpenter sugirió que el holotipo de Nanotyrannus lancensis podría ser inmaduro y, siguiendo a Rozhdestvensky, lo interpretó como un juvenil de T. rex.

facts.statement: Many paleontologists, including Phil Currie and Donald M. Henderson, concluded that Nanotyrannus was a juvenile T. rex or a closely related species.
facts.quote: Muchos paleontólogos, como Phil Currie y Donald M. Henderson, que examinaron a Jane concluyeron que el Nanotyrannus fue un T. rex juvenil o una especie muy cercana.

facts.statement: Other researchers, such as Peter Larson, continue to support Nanotyrannus as a separate genus.
facts.quote: Otros, como Peter Larson, continúan apoyando un género separado para Nanotyrannus.

facts.statement: The genus Nanotyrannus was named by Bakker and colleagues in 1988.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Nanotyrannus (genus), Bakker et al. 1988

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus is classified within the family Nanotyrannidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Nanotyrannidae

facts.statement: Nanotyrannus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2026 study based on bone histology found that the growth trajectories of Nanotyrannus specimens did not fit the growth curve model of adult T. rex, suggesting a distinct subadult stage.
facts.quote: Woodward, Myhrvold & Horner (2026) reconstruct the life history of Tyrannosaurus on the basis of bone histology, reporting evidence of a more gradual annual growth rate slope than indicated by earlier studies and evidence of a protracted subadult stage, and find that growth trajectories of the tyrannosaur specimens BMRP 2002.4.1 (the holotype of Nanotyrannus lethaeus) and BMRP 2006.4.4 did not fit the T. rex growth curve model.

rejected.statement: A 2025 study by Griffin et al. used hyoid bone histology to argue the holotype was mature, but this methodology was questioned in 2026 by Woodruff et al.
rejected.quote: An independent study by Christopher T. Griffin and colleagues published later that year argued that the holotype skull of N. lancensis belonged to a mature individual based on histology (microscopic study of the living organism's tissue) of the hyoid bone, but D. Cary Woodruff and colleagues questioned their methodology for hyoid bone histology in 2026.
rejected.reason: numbers not in the quote: ['2025']

rejected.statement: Adult N. lancensis may have weighed nearly 704 kilograms based on the "Bloody Mary" specimen.
rejected.quote: The adult N. lancensis may have weighed nearly 704 kg based on the "Bloody Mary" specimen.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Adult N lancensis may have weighed nearly 704'

rejected.statement: Mature individuals of N. lethaeus may have reached a body mass of about 1200 kilograms.
